title: Security fault matrix
description: Objective: run hostile credentials, stale authority, command replay, corruption, crash-at-boundary, poison, resource, and provider fault schedules across the full system. Deliverable: security/fault fixtures and exact evidence. NOT in scope: host-malicious sandbox claims. Hard dependencies: Schedule coverage checker and all production adapters. Owned paths: tests/security/** and tests/fault/**. Verification: pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security.
definitionOfDone: Every declared authority and external-effect boundary has hostile before/after/race coverage.
No unauthorized mutation, duplicate effect, budget mint, hidden skip, or false evidence acceptance occurs.
Unobservable host behavior is labeled outside-scope or UNKNOWN precisely.
taskRails: Claims follow the benchmark permit-list; missing, partial, cross-basis, or unverifiable evidence is UNKNOWN, never PASS.
No confirmatory corpus is generated or viewed until the implementation commit is frozen exactly as specified.
GO_QUIESCE and GO_ACTIVATE are separate human decisions. Keep evidence exact, reproducible, and scoped to one source commit.

comments.author: architect-5b5302ee
comments.content:
Expanded planning audit (2026-08-09, HEAD 7afa17d), preserving the BLOCKED verdict.

This task is also too broad for one <=60-minute implementation slice once its production subjects exist: the committed tree currently exposes at least eight security surfaces and eight fault surfaces. Re-plan it as the FINAL integration/hardening proof after these file-disjoint test slices land:

1. Authority transport hostile matrix — tests/security/transports/**. Drive public production ingress for daemon HTTP/event stream, MCP stdio/Streamable HTTP, authenticated IDE/control-room, importer, and force paths. Case rows cover missing/malformed/expired/revoked/swapped/replayed credentials and stale version/epoch/binding/command/artifact identities. Each row pins exact stable code AND refusing layer/stage and reads authoritative state/effect/budget/audit deltas back as zero. Generated rows assert non-zero count and exact set equality with the production registry.
2. Integrity/scope hostile matrix — tests/security/integrity/**. Drive production path/scope, symlink/junction/submodule/UNC/device/case, malicious Git ref, argv/env, N/N+1 bounds, provider-closure swap, evidence substitution/tamper, redaction and distribution handshake surfaces. Same code/layer and zero-authority assertions; same production-registry non-vacuity ratchet.
3. Durable-store fault matrix — tests/fault/store/**. Real SQLite/subprocess schedules at transaction begin/write/commit/ack, WAL/checkpoint, corruption/permission/lock, outbox/inbox/projection poison and replay. Assert whole-or-none durable truth, exact STORE/OUTBOX code+layer, command replay idempotency, no lost acknowledged event, and no duplicate delivery. Test-produced helpers must not replace relay/controller production entry points.
4. Runtime/provider fault matrix — tests/fault/runtime/**. Drive production dispatcher/supervisor/platform/provider/resource/budget/artifact composition before/after/race at registration, lock, activation, physical start, result, ack, cancel and recovery. Assert one authoritative effect, no budget mint/slot/resource duplication, exact recovery/refusal code+layer, and honest UNKNOWN for unobservable host facts. Host-malicious same-user behavior is explicitly OUTSIDE_SCOPE, never PASS or skip.
5. Gate-lane wiring prerequisite — root package.json plus tests/fault/tsconfig.json and tests/security/tsconfig.json. Shell-neutral scripts must run strict tsc over all tests/** lane files before Vitest: pnpm test:fault and pnpm test:security. Root recursive typecheck does not cover tests/** today.
6. This task then owns the full-matrix ratchet and final proof only: verify every prerequisite shipping task is DONE and reachable from a real consumer, exact design/benchmark hashes and one source commit, no confirmatory corpus bytes, exhaustive production registry ↔ executed-case set equality, exact UNKNOWN/outside-scope rows, and one adversarial mutation per refusal layer plus one deleted-case non-vacuity mutation.
7. Final verification is exactly pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security, followed by the epic-required path-attributed repo baseline comparison; no generated evidence file is committed.

Current missing subjects, verified on disk: daemon HTTP has injected Authenticator/DecisionPort but no real composition/root export; core authenticateCommand has test-only callers; event stream has no auth/listener; MCP stdio/HTTP have no daemon dispatch/session port (HTTP internals are not root-exported); importer has no authenticated command/store composition; control room main mounts fixtures; R3/force handlers are absent; outbox relay is internal/unconsumed; activateEffect/platform launcher/OS lock are unconsumed or absent; provider probes do not spawn/pin processes; budget settlement/artifact concrete edges are unconsumed; J3/J4 are in flight; Codex/JetBrains/distribution/platform prerequisites are not DONE. The schedule checker is DONE but its 10 refs are abstract categories, not an exhaustive production boundary registry.

Do not submit the parent plan until the new production-prerequisite task IDs are known; Clause 2 requires naming those shipping tasks in the acceptance plan. Preserve existing tests/fault/foundation/** (task-18c7921 DONE) and avoid disaster-restore/Linux/macOS owned subtrees.

comments.content:
Second planning pass: concrete SPIDR child specifications and the eventual parent plan. These are blueprints only; do not create duplicates while architect-1721c07f owns prerequisite authoring.

CHILD A — Authority transport hostile schedules
- Owned files: tests/security/transports/authority-cases.ts, authority-matrix.test.ts, tsconfig.json.
- Objective/deliverable: a frozen, registry-derived matrix that drives the composed production daemon HTTP/event, MCP stdio/Streamable HTTP, control-room/IDE, importer, and R3 force entry points; no injected test-only authority port may stand in for a missing consumer edge.
- DoD: (1) case universe is non-empty and exact-set-equal to the versioned production authority registry, with BEFORE/AFTER/RACE for every boundary; (2) missing/malformed/expired/revoked/swapped/replayed credentials plus stale version/epoch/binding/command/artifact rows assert exact code and refusing layer/stage; (3) each refusal reads the authoritative store/effect/budget/audit surfaces and proves zero mutation/effect/mint while valid stale rejections are redacted/audited; (4) multiple-layer controls pin which layer refused and mutation of each layer makes its named row red; (5) pnpm exec tsc -p tests/security/transports/tsconfig.json && pnpm exec vitest run tests/security/transports exits 0.
- Not in scope: filesystem/provider integrity and effect crash scheduling.

CHILD B — Integrity boundary hostile schedules
- Owned files: tests/security/integrity/integrity-cases.ts, integrity-matrix.test.ts, tsconfig.json.
- Production surfaces: runner observeScope/createNodeScopePaths/createNodeGitObserver, workspace manifests, concrete artifact store, provider runtime closure/render/evidence validation, importer canonicalization, and signed distribution handshake.
- DoD: (1) production-registry exact-set equality plus non-zero N/N+1 rows; (2) path traversal, symlink/junction/submodule/UNC/device/case collision, malicious Git refs, argv/env injection, oversize, provider path swap, artifact/evidence substitution and tamper assert exact code+layer; (3) no hostile bytes, provider output, or evidence grant command/effect/lease/verification authority; (4) same-user malicious-host behavior is explicitly OUTSIDE_SCOPE/UNKNOWN, never skipped or PASS; (5) pnpm exec tsc -p tests/security/integrity/tsconfig.json && pnpm exec vitest run tests/security/integrity exits 0.
- Cross-platform: use Node path APIs and real platform observations; never POSIX quoting, /tmp, or fake signal claims.

CHILD C — Durable store fault schedules
- Owned files: tests/fault/store/store-fault-cases.ts, store-fault-matrix.test.ts, tsconfig.json.
- Production surfaces: public SqliteEventStore plus the future exported/consumed transactional relay; real SQLite/subprocess injection, never an in-memory reimplementation.
- DoD: (1) registry-derived BEFORE/AFTER/RACE cases cover transaction begin/write/commit/ack, WAL/checkpoint, disk/permission/lock/corruption, outbox/inbox/projection poison/replay; (2) every failure pins exact STORE/OUTBOX code+layer and reads whole-or-none durable state; (3) replays produce one decision/effect/delivery and acknowledged facts are not lost; (4) generated count is non-zero/exact and a removed boundary or neutralized production guard reddens the named row; (5) pnpm exec tsc -p tests/fault/store/tsconfig.json && pnpm exec vitest run tests/fault/store exits 0.

CHILD D — Runtime effect fault schedules
- Owned files: tests/fault/runtime/runtime-fault-cases.ts, runtime-fault-matrix.test.ts, tsconfig.json.
- Production surfaces: composed dispatcher, runner activateEffect/consumeActivationGrant/validateActivationCommit, platform lock/process boundary, classifyCrash/admitResume, Claude/Codex adapters, scheduler resource/provider-slot/budget authority, and concrete artifact store.
- DoD: (1) exact production-registry cases cover registration, claim, lock, activation, physical start, result, ack, cancel, invalidate and recovery in BEFORE/AFTER/RACE orderings; (2) provider death/hang/truncate/corrupt/path-swap and resource UNKNOWN cross-products assert stable reason+layer and precise recovery set; (3) one authoritative effect, no duplicate launch/resource/slot/budget spend, and no hidden skip are proven by durable read-back; (4) off-host physical facts remain typed UNKNOWN; host-malicious behavior remains outside scope; (5) pnpm exec tsc -p tests/fault/runtime/tsconfig.json && pnpm exec vitest run tests/fault/runtime exits 0.

CHILD E — Fault/security gate lane
- Owned files (scope amendment required): package.json, tests/fault/tsconfig.json, tests/security/tsconfig.json.

- DoD: all lane files are covered by strict NodeNext compilation, discovery is non-zero, pnpm test:fault and pnpm test:security both exit 0 on Windows, and no POSIX-only syntax is introduced.

EVENTUAL PARENT task-05ce9b8f plan (2 new aggregate test files, <=7 steps)
1. Re-verify pinned design/benchmark hashes, frozen source commit, and every named production/test prerequisite task DONE and consumer-reachable; no edits and no confirmatory corpus access.
2. RED tests in tests/security/system/security-coverage.test.ts: import child case manifests plus the production security registry and require exact two-way set equality, every boundary's BEFORE/AFTER/RACE phases, non-zero counts, unique identities, exact code+layer, and permitted UNKNOWN/outside-scope only.
3. RED tests in tests/fault/system/fault-coverage.test.ts: same ratchet for the production fault/effect registry and schedule-checker boundary mapping; no abstract category may claim PASS without executed production evidence.
4. Implement only the minimal aggregate fixture wiring in those two files; do not patch production or weaken a child expectation. A discovered production defect becomes a named prerequisite task.
5. One adversarial pass: neutralize one production refusal per layer and require the corresponding test to fail; remove one generated case in-memory and require exact-set/non-vacuity failure; restore by exact committed hash.
6. Single final verification step: record repo-wide baseline/HEAD path-attributed failures, then run the task's exact fresh command pnpm test:fault && pnpm test:security; owned lanes must be exit 0.

comments.author: architect-5b5302ee
comments.content:
Third planning pass: exact prerequisite probes, case contract, oracles, and mutation plan. This extends the handoff only; governor msg-a973ed5907cc4925943b8d7a6a67e885 explicitly says the unknown PLANNING flip did not resolve the block.

A. Re-plan admission checklist — every row must be true at one committed source SHA before submitting the parent plan:
1. Daemon authority composition: a non-test production caller binds core authenticateCommand, daemon buildCommandRegistry/handleCommandRequest, and SqliteEventStore/decision application. Today authenticateCommand and handleCommandRequest have test-only callers and handleCommandRequest is absent from the daemon root.
2. Event transport composition: readEventPage/resumeFromSnapshot are behind authenticated byte/listener ingress and a real SubscriptionPort; today they are root-exported kernels with no auth/listener composition.
3. MCP composition: @moe/mcp root exposes both stable stdio and Streamable HTTP entry points and production StdioDispatchPort/HttpDispatchPort/HttpSessionPort implementations call the daemon. Today HTTP internals are sealed and both transports rely on injected ports.
4. Import composition: applyImport is reachable from an authenticated daemon/CLI command over a copied frozen source plus a real store transaction; today only package tests consume it.
5. Control-room/IDE composition: production main mounts createDataAdapter with a real DaemonTransport/session/event stream, and the JetBrains adapter is landed; today main mounts fixture state and adapters/ is absent.
6. Force/R3 composition: durable authenticated handlers exist for lease.confirm_revoke, resource.confirm_released, budget.conservative_settle, budget.acknowledge_unknown_liability, recovery.complete and cutover commands, enforcing recent step-up and reason; today vocabulary/builders/doctor proposals are zero-authority shapes.
7. Store relay composition: relayMessage is public and has a durable production consumer; today it is package-internal and consumed only by tests/drill helpers.
8. Effect/platform composition: a production dispatcher calls activateEffect, consumes/validates the one-use grant, registers an OS lock/process, and persists outcome/ack; packages/runner/src/platform exists for every supported OS. Today no dispatcher/platform directory/OS lock exists.
9. Provider composition: Claude/Codex process launch, runtime-closure pin, signal/cancel and observation paths have production callers, not only probe/render/stream kernels.
10. Resource/budget/artifact composition: adapterConfirm/adapterFail, budget account/measurement/settlement, provider-slot/resource transitions and createArtifactStore have durable production consumers; today several are internal or test-only.
11. Distribution and host prerequisites: distribution manifest packaging is DONE; real supported-host runs exist for host claims. Off-host stays UNKNOWN.
12. Gate lane: package.json owns shell-neutral test:fault/test:security scripts, both lane tsconfigs compile every discovered file, and tests/fault/foundation plus disaster/Linux/macOS ownership is explicitly preserved.
13. Boundary universe: a versioned production-derived authority/effect registry is public and consumed. The schedule checker’s 10 abstract refs alone do not meet this condition.
14. Every shipping task id for rows 1-13 is named and DONE. REVIEW/WORKING/untracked bytes are not prerequisites.

Cheap probes for the next architect:
- rg with --glob !**/*.test.ts for authenticateCommand(, handleCommandRequest(, createHttpMcpAdapter(, applyImport(, createDataAdapter(, relayMessage(, activateEffect(, consumeActivationGrant(, createArtifactStore(, adapterConfirm( and adapterFail(; each must show a durable consumer, not only its definition.
- Test-Path packages/runner/src/platform and enumerate linux/macos/windows implementation files.
- Plain-Node package-root Object.keys probes for @moe/daemon, @moe/mcp, @moe/import and @moe/runner; Vitest resolution is not loadability evidence.
- Read package.json scripts and run tsc -p for both lane configs; root pnpm typecheck does not reach tests/**.

B. Shared case-manifest contract for each child
Each frozen case carries: caseId, productionBoundaryId, abstractScheduleBoundaryRef, entryPoint, faultClass, phase BEFORE|AFTER|RACE, applicableHost, expectedOutcome REFUSED|UNKNOWN|OUTSIDE_SCOPE, expectedCode, expectedLayer, beforeSnapshotDigest, afterSnapshotOracle, auditOracle, and sourceTaskId. IDs canonicalize actor/effect/resource roles and exclude random ids, timestamps and seed labels. For every production boundary:
- applicableFaults is non-empty;
- all three phases exist;
- caseIds and canonical identities are unique;
- generatedCount equals executedCount and is greater than zero;
- registry minus case ids and cases minus registry both equal empty;
- expectedCode is a member of the production closed vocabulary and expectedLayer is a production layer, never a test-local substitute.
UNKNOWN/OUTSIDE_SCOPE rows still execute a production observation and assert the precise code/layer; no it.skip, it.todo, conditional return, or unreadable result may count as evidence.

C. Required state oracles
1. Unauthorized refusal: compare authoritative aggregate version/event/outbox/decision/effect/resource/provider-slot/budget/audit digests before and after; every mutable delta is zero except the explicitly required redacted rejection audit row.
2. Command/outbox replay: same command/effect id yields one decision, one authoritative effect and one deduplicated delivery; conflict uses its exact code/layer.
3. Budget/resource conservation: sum of available+reserved+active+unknown liability cannot increase, slot/resource holder count never exceeds capacity, and UNKNOWN release cannot fund a successor.
4. Crash boundary: after restart, durable state is whole-or-none, one exact recovery classification/set is offered, and running cannot be inferred from silence.
5. Evidence/provider integrity: byte/digest/closure mismatch is refused before activation/acceptance and no provider output grants verification authority.
6. Hidden-skip guard: generated identities equal observed result identities, counts are non-zero, and any unreadable/aborted schedule is UNKNOWN/FAIL evidence rather than silently omitted.

D. Adversarial mutation allocation
- Authority child: neutralize authentication, capability, stale-epoch and replay guards one at a time; each must redden the row naming that code and layer.
- Integrity child: neutralize canonical-path, runtime-closure and evidence-digest checks; each must redden its production entry-point row.
- Store child: neutralize rollback/expected-version/outbox-inbox dedupe checks without causing syntax failure; whole-or-none or duplicate oracle must red.
- Runtime child: permit grant reuse, UNKNOWN resource release, duplicate provider launch or budget reservation; exact effect/resource/budget oracle must red.
- Parent: remove one case from each manifest and alter one UNKNOWN to PASS; exact-set/non-vacuity and truth-lattice tests must red. Restore every production path by its pre-mutation committed blob hash and rerun green.

No plan may use a helper that recomputes production authority. The production surface supplies result, code, layer and state; tests only snapshot, invoke, and compare.

comments.author: architect-5b5302ee
comments.content:
Fourth planning pass: remove two latent plan defects — gate cycles and accidental root-suite execution — and define the boundary-catalog architecture.

1. Dedicated test tiers, not ordinary *.test.ts
New hostile/process/fault files use *.security.ts and *.fault.ts. Root vitest.config.ts discovers only **/*.test.ts, so these lanes do not silently join every worker's ordinary pnpm test. Existing tests/fault/foundation/*.test.ts remain included in both the ordinary root suite and the dedicated fault config.
- tests/fault/vitest.config.ts includes tests/fault/**/*.test.ts plus tests/fault/**/*.fault.ts, node environment, sequential execution, passWithNoTests false.
- tests/security/vitest.config.ts includes tests/security/**/*.security.ts, node environment, sequential execution, passWithNoTests false.
- focused commands always pass --config; plain vitest run tests/security/... would use the root include and can discover zero files.
- lane tsconfigs include every .ts recursively and extend the strict root base.

2. Corrected lane ordering (the earlier single Child E created a cycle)
G0 Fault-lane infrastructure lands first because committed Foundation tests make the lane non-empty: owns package.json, tests/fault/tsconfig.json, tests/fault/vitest.config.ts; adds test:fault = tsc -p tests/fault/tsconfig.json && vitest run --config tests/fault/vitest.config.ts; verification pnpm test:fault.
S1 Authority-security child then creates tests/security/tsconfig.json, tests/security/vitest.config.ts, authority-cases.ts, authority-matrix.security.ts and verifies via direct tsc + configured Vitest. It does not claim a root security gate yet.
G1 Security-lane wiring runs immediately after S1 and owns only package.json; adds test:security = tsc -p tests/security/tsconfig.json && vitest run --config tests/security/vitest.config.ts; verification pnpm test:security.
S2 integrity security and F1/F2 store/runtime fault children then run file-disjoint in their owned subdirectories against the established lanes.
P parent aggregate runs last.
This prevents a green empty security script and gives Linux/macOS/disaster tasks a real test:fault command without waiting for the whole matrix. package.json edits are sequenced, never concurrent.

3. Revised child filenames
- tests/security/transports/authority-cases.ts + authority-matrix.security.ts
- tests/security/integrity/integrity-cases.ts + integrity-matrix.security.ts
- tests/fault/store/store-fault-cases.ts + store-fault-matrix.fault.ts
- tests/fault/runtime/runtime-fault-cases.ts + runtime-fault-matrix.fault.ts
- parent: tests/security/system/security-coverage.security.ts + tests/fault/system/fault-coverage.fault.ts
Case files are imported support, not independently discovered. Each discovered file asserts the imported case count > 0.

4. No-hidden-skip enforcement
The two parent coverage files use the TypeScript compiler API (already a dev dependency) to parse all lane sources and reject actual call expressions using it/test/describe.skip, todo, skipIf or runIf; do not grep text/comments. They assert scanned-file and checked-call counts >0. Runtime generatedCount===executedIdentitySet.size catches conditional early returns and unreadable subprocess results. UNREADABLE/ABORT are explicit evidence classifications, never skipped.

5. Production boundary catalog architecture (avoids reversing package dependencies)
Do not put a hand-authored “whole system” list in testkit or contracts. Contracts may define only the frozen BoundaryDescriptor codec/version. Each production subsystem exports its own catalog from the same module that exposes the entry point or protocol registry. The signed distribution manifest enumerates installed components plus each component catalog digest. The final matrix:
- reads the distribution component set;
- loads every required component catalog from its public production root;
- proves component-set ↔ catalog-set equality and catalog digest equality;
- maps every catalog row to executed cases;
- proves each entry-point/protocol registry’s local exact-set guard in that component’s own package tests.
A new component without a catalog or a catalog without a distribution binding therefore fails closed. Contracts never import consumers, and testkit never authors authority.

BoundaryDescriptor minimum fields: registryVersion, boundaryId, componentId, category AUTHORITY|EXTERNAL_EFFECT|INTEGRITY, publicEntryPoint, abstractScheduleBoundaryRef (one of the schedule checker’s 10 categories), supportedPhases, applicableFaultClasses, stableCodes, stableLayers, hostObservability OBSERVABLE|HOST_DEPENDENT|HOST_MALICIOUS_OUT_OF_SCOPE, and catalogDigest. Governance task ids stay in the acceptance handoff/evidence, not production bytes.

6. Evidence identity
Canonical case identity hashes boundaryId, phase, faultClass, actor/effect/resource role and happens-before edges; it excludes random ids, wall time and seed labels. Each manifest is DEVELOPMENT_ONLY_ENGINEERING_EVIDENCE with confirmatory:false and contains no BENCH identifiers. The verbose lane summary prints component-catalog digests, case-manifest digest, generated/executed counts and explicit UNKNOWN/OUTSIDE_SCOPE counts, but never credentials, raw provider output or physical paths. HEAD/source attribution remains completion evidence rather than a self-referential hash embedded in committed source.

7. Dependency DAG
Production descriptor contract -> subsystem catalogs/real consumer edges -> distribution catalog binding.
In parallel after those land: G0, then S1 and F1/F2 as their production subjects allow; G1 after S1; S2 after its distribution/provider subjects; parent P after G1+S1+S2+F1+F2 plus disaster/Linux/macOS/JetBrains/distribution tasks DONE.
No child edits tests/fault/foundation, tests/fault/disaster-restore, tests/fault/linux or tests/fault/macos.
